patterns_data.top_pattern: DSNP and SNP claims in the Not Mapped facility bucket are the largest spend driver
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: DSNP HMO and SNP Crossover / Not Mapped facility claims
patterns_data.pattern_details: A very large share of the increase is sitting in the Not Mapped facility bucket, led by IN DSNP HMO and supported by smaller but similar spikes in TX, CA, CO, and TX SNP Crossover. Because the claims are not tied to a usable facility category, the current result blends utilization, site-of-care, and reimbursement effects. This should be treated as a gating validation issue before broad authorization, network, or pricing action is taken.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is the single largest pattern and can misdirect both utilization management and provider action if the claims are not first assigned to the right facility bucket.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a focused claims-mapping correction for Not Mapped facility claims in IN DSNP HMO first, then TX/CA/CO DSNP HMO and TX SNP Crossover, and only then re-run provider and site-of-care action planning.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Facility attribution is missing on the main claims driving the increase, so root-cause attribution is not reliable until mapping is corrected.
evidence_summary: IN DSNP HMO Not Mapped claims increased by +$50.5M across 94,559 claims, with paid per admit up about $192.
CA/CO/TX DSNP HMO Not Mapped claims added +$3.7M, with TX contributing +$3.6M and 7,082 more claims.
TX SNP Crossover Not Mapped claims added another +$675K across 5,458 claims.
All contributing groups were flagged for unmapped or unknown values and repeated concentration.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Large unattributed outpatient spend is concentrated in temporary-code and not-mapped categories
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: UNATTRIBUTED / OP HH/DME and OP Mgmt Oth Misc
patterns_data.pattern_details: A large unattributed outpatient increase is concentrated in OP HH/DME and OP Mgmt Oth Misc, tied to R69 and temporary or national code groupings. The mix of unattributed claims, not-mapped categories, and temporary codes makes this look more like coding, classification, or feed drift than a clean utilization trend. Validate attribution and code mapping before changing outpatient authorization rules.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is the second-largest dollar pattern and could drive the wrong outpatient policy response if it is treated as true utilization growth.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Audit the UNATTRIBUTED outpatient feed for R69, temporary national codes, and national T codes; correct attribution and benefit mapping, then reassess whether any real utilization or unit-cost issue remains.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in unattributed claims and temporary or not-mapped outpatient coding, so business action should wait for coding and attribution cleanup.
evidence_summary: UNATTRIBUTED OP HH/DME increased by +$25.4M across 32,835 claims, tied to R69 and Temporary National Codes (Non-Medicare).
UNATTRIBUTED OP Mgmt Oth Misc added +$16.9M across 47,830 claims, split between Temporary National Codes (Non-Medicare) and National T Codes.
Both groups were flagged for not-mapped values, repeated concentration, and low-baseline behavior.
The pattern is concentrated enough to warrant data cleanup before operational action.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Post-acute spend is rising, led by Indiana home health with smaller SNF and NF outliers
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: DSNP HMO / Home Health, SNF, and NF post-acute services
patterns_data.pattern_details: Post-acute pressure is being driven mainly by Indiana DSNP home health, with smaller skilled nursing and nursing facility outlier cases across IN, TX, and VA. This points to a site-of-care and provider-mix issue in post-acute services rather than a broad acute inpatient trend. The main business levers are authorization pathway design, discharge steering, and provider rate review in post-acute settings.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Post-acute placement decisions can scale quickly, so early action on home health and skilled nursing can prevent a broader cost trend.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review DSNP post-acute authorization and discharge pathways in IN first, then validate provider-specific SNF and NF outliers in TX and IN for placement appropriateness and contracted rate accuracy.
evidence_summary: IN DSNP HMO home health increased by +$5.4M across 8,268 claims, with paid per admit up about $635.
DSNP HMO SNF claims across IN/TX/VA added +$72K, concentrated at PROVENA SACRED HEART HOME and THE RENAISSANCE AT KESSLER PARK.
NF rare cases across IN/TX added +$72K, led by Organic Disturbances and Intellectual Disability, Osteomyelitis with MCC, and Pulmonary Edema and Respiratory Failure.
The smaller SNF and NF signals are low volume, but they support the broader post-acute concentration story.
